d: Soluble fms-like tyrosine kinase 1, a decoy VEGF receptor released by the ischemic placenta; it traps VEGF and placental growth factor and causes the maternal endothelial injury of preeclampsia.
Hemolysis, elevated liver enzymes and low platelets, a severe form of preeclampsia that can appear with only mildly raised blood pressure; delivery is the treatment.
A syncytiotrophoblast hormone that rises with placental mass and causes maternal insulin resistance and lipolysis, sparing glucose for the fetus; it underlies gestational diabetes.
Abnormally deep placental attachment where decidua is missing, usually over a cesarean scar: accreta attaches to myometrium, increta invades it and percreta passes through it.
An acid-elution blood smear that counts fetal red cells, which resist acid because of hemoglobin F, to measure fetomaternal hemorrhage and set the anti-D immune globulin dose.
